title: AgentConnect Public Schema (pre-1.0 draft)
description: Generated from schema.ts. Do not edit by hand. Run npm run generate.

AgentConnectPublicSchema.description: Root used only to generate one JSON Schema containing every public object. Applications exchange the referenced objects, not this wrapper.

Address.description: Agent Address accepted by the grammar in addressing.md. The location, when present, is one or more dot-separated DNS labels. The Runtime canonicalizes ASCII uppercase to lowercase. Examples: `writer`, `writer@content-squad`, `writer@legal.acme.com`.

QualifiedAddress.description: Canonical Address stored in Runtime-owned output. Both parts are lowercase and the location is always present. The location is one or more dot-separated DNS labels, so this type already represents a remote Address such as `writer@legal.acme.com`. A single-Team Runtime only ever emits a single-label location equal to its own Team name.

CollectMode.description:
How the sender collects the result of a request. It is a choice made on the `send` call and is not stored on the immutable Message; the recipient never observes it. Every request send carries `collect` and opens a Ticket. The send may omit `deadline`; the accepted Request Message always carries the effective cutoff the Runtime stamped. An event is the fire-and-forget kind and names neither.

- `wait`: keep `send` open until the Ticket is terminal or `wait_hold_seconds` elapses, then return the current Ticket. That Ticket may still be `open`.
- `ticket`: return the current Ticket immediately. That Ticket may be `open` or already terminal.

DeliveryHistoryForm.description:
How a Session wants Thread history attached to each Delivery.

- `bodies`: include earlier Message objects (the default).
- `ids`: include only earlier Message ids. The Agent pages bodies with   `get_history`.

ErrorCode.description: Well-known public error codes. `ErrorObject.code` is this closed set. An Agent application failure code belongs in `ErrorObject.details`.

SkillExample.description: Short natural-language example of using a Skill. Examples are illustrative text, not typed contracts, because a request to an Agent is free-form `content`, not a call against a declared signature.

name.description: Stable lowercase identifier, unique within the Profile. It is not an Address or a Runtime operation name.

description.description: Direct description of what the Skill does.

examples.description: Concrete natural-language examples used for discovery and reader understanding.

tags.description: Optional lowercase labels scoped to this Skill. They appear only on the full Profile, not on the light DirectoryMatch card.

Skill.description:
One thing an Agent claims it can do, described in natural language.

A Skill has no input or output schema. An Agent is addressed as one conversational participant; a caller describes the work in `content` and does not target a typed Skill signature. Skills exist to make discovery specific and to render an Agent's abilities to a reader, not to define an RPC surface.

summary.description: Short description used on the light DirectoryMatch card.

description.description: Longer optional explanation of suitable work and boundaries. Present on the full Profile from `get_profiles`, not on the light `find` card.

skills.description: One or more Skills. Names must be unique within this array.

tags.description: Lowercase discovery labels for the Agent as a whole. They appear on the light DirectoryMatch card. Duplicate tags are invalid.

AgentProfile.description:
Discovery information for an Agent.

A Profile describes what one participant can do, the way a short bio describes a person. Identity, name, Address, presence, and Session data do not belong here; the DirectoryEntry owns identity and addressing.

code.description: Well-known ErrorCode. An Agent application failure code belongs in `details` of a `handler_failed` error, whose shape the Agent owns.

details.description: Optional structured data safe to reveal to the requester.

retryable.description: Whether repeating the failed action may succeed without changing input.

ErrorObject.description: Public failure data. Runtime errors and Agent handler failures share this shape so Clients can handle them consistently.

details.description: Optional structured data safe to reveal to the requester.

retryable.description: Whether repeating the failed action may succeed without changing input.

DeadlineExceededError.description: Error stored by an expired Ticket.

id.description: Immutable Message id and idempotency key. Client-proposed on `send` or `reply`, then stored unchanged when the Runtime accepts the Message.

sender.description: Canonical qualified Address set by the Runtime.

sender_did.description: Verified DID of the sending Membership, copied from the authenticated Session at acceptance. It is not looked up later from the Directory. A principal, including `operator`, has a DID and this field carries it.

recipient.description: Canonical qualified Address set by the Runtime.

trace_id.description: Correlation id shared by every Message in one causal exchange. The Runtime assigns a new value to a root Message and copies it onto every Message caused by it, so one `trace_id` reconstructs a whole timeline.

thread_id.description: Optional Thread grouping id.

parent_id.description: Message this one replies to or continues. Singular: the Message relation is a tree. A response or error MUST name the request. A follow-up in the same Thread MAY name a prior Message in that Thread. A send that creates a new Thread MAY name an authorized parent from another Thread so the child copies `trace_id`. A result merged from several answers names one parent. Shared `trace_id` correlates the operation; it does not record which subset of answers were consumed.

seq.description: Position of this Message in its Thread, assigned on acceptance. Present exactly when `thread_id` is present. The first accepted Message in a Thread is `1`. Each later Message, including a response or error, receives the next integer. History, the delivered window, and `before` cursors order by this value, not by `created_at`. A Message with `thread_id` and no `seq`, or `seq` and no `thread_id`, is invalid. The generated JSON Schema encodes that with a oneOf on each Message kind.

kind.description: Identifies work sent to an Agent.

metadata.description: Sender-controlled application data. Never used for Runtime decisions.

deadline.description: Absolute time after which an open Ticket expires.

RequestMessage.description: Request that always expects a reply. It carries a `deadline`, opens a Ticket, and ends in a terminal Ticket state. Fire-and-forget work is an `event`.

Uuid.description: RFC 9562 UUID used for Messages, Threads, leases, traces, and Instances.

AgentDid.description: Agent-owned `did:key` identity backed by an Ed25519 public key.

Timestamp.description: UTC RFC 3339 timestamp with a trailing `Z`. Example: `2026-08-18T15:00:00Z`.

history.description: Bounded recent window of earlier Messages from this Thread. Empty when the Session joined with `delivery_history=ids`; then `history_ids` carries the window.

history_ids.description: Earlier Message ids when this Session joined with `delivery_history=ids`. Omitted when the window is Message bodies.

history_complete.description: True when the delivered window already contains every earlier retained Message.

Delivery.description:
One exclusive attempt to handle a Message.

`history` is a bounded recent window of the Thread, ordered by `seq` ascending and excluding `message`. The window is capped by `delivery_history_limit` and, when it carries Message bodies, by `max_message_bytes`. A Session that joined with `delivery_history=ids` receives `history_ids` instead of bodies. When `history_complete` is false, older retained Messages exist and can be paged with `get_history`.

DeclinedTicket.description: Ticket the recipient deliberately declined. The recipient handled the request and chose not to answer, the way a person may read a message and decide no reply is warranted. It is a terminal, non-failure outcome that is explicit to the requester, distinct from a handler failure and from a deadline that expired with no handling.

TicketViewError.description: Lean failure on a model-facing Ticket view. Code and message only; no details, retryable flag, or Message envelope.

ticket_id.description: Request Message id. The only id on this view.

thread_id.description: Thread the request belongs to, when it has one. Reuse this with the same recipient.

TicketViewBase.description: Fields shared by every model-facing Ticket view. MCP `ask` / `get_result` and Session-bound Team tools return this projection, not the wire Ticket. Runtime, HTTP, and Client `ask` / `get_result` still return the wire Ticket. Branch on `state`. Timing is not proof of state.

ticket_id.description: Request Message id. The only id on this view.

thread_id.description: Thread the request belongs to, when it has one. Reuse this with the same recipient.

state.description: Ticket still waiting for its first accepted outcome. Keep `ticket_id` and call `get_result`.

deadline.description: Absolute work cutoff stamped at acceptance. Not an ETA, not a wait bound, and not proof of `state`.

poll_interval_ms.description: Hint for how often to call `get_result` while `state` is open. Not a wait bound, work duration, or lease change. Do not send a new ask to collect.

status_message.description: Next action while open: keep `ticket_id` and call `get_result`; do not send a new ask.

agent_did.description: Stable identity supplied by the Membership.

DirectoryEntry.description: Full Directory record for one Membership. Runtime `get_profile` returns this object: Address, DID, and Profile together. It is not a bare Profile.

address.description: Canonical qualified Address to send work to.

skill_names.description: Declared Skill names, for a cheap capability scan.

tags.description: Profile tags. Skill tags are not copied onto this card.

DirectoryMatch.description: One ranked discovery result. Light on purpose so a search can list a whole Team without flooding a model's context. Read selected Profiles with `get_profiles`.

ProfileView.description: Address and Profile without Directory DID bookkeeping. Runtime, HTTP, and Client `get_profile` / `get_entry` still return `DirectoryEntry`.

ProfileFound.description: Found item in `GetProfilesResult`. `address` is the canonical Directory Address, which may differ in qualification from the requested string.

ProfileMiss.description: Missing or unauthorized item in `GetProfilesResult`. `address` is the requested string. `error` uses the same codes as a single Runtime lookup.

GetProfilesResult.description: Model-facing `get_profiles` result. `items` follow the requested order after duplicate requested strings are dropped, keeping the first.

status.description: Discriminator for an accepted notice. No Ticket is created. This is not proof the recipient has processed the event.

thread_id.description: Conversation this event joined, when it has one.

TellView.description: Model-facing `tell` result. MCP and Session-bound Team tools return this projection, not the wire `AcceptedSendResult`. `status: accepted` means the Runtime queued the event, not that the recipient finished processing. `thread_id` is present only when the event joined a Thread.

nonce.description: At least 128 bits of random data in base64url form.

audience.description: Exact JWT audience required by the Runtime.

expires_at.description: Time after which this challenge cannot authenticate a join.

JoinChallenge.description: Short-lived challenge used to prove Agent DID control.

spec_version.description: Exact public contract version implemented by the Client.

name.description: Requested Agent name, canonicalized by the Runtime.

profile.description: Discovery information that replaces the Membership's current Profile.

instance_id.description: Stable id for one running copy of the Agent. It MUST be unique per running copy. Re-joining with the same `instance_id` replaces that Instance's Session; a different value opens an additional concurrent Instance sharing the Membership and Mailbox. Omit to let the Runtime assign one.

max_in_flight.description: Maximum active Delivery leases for this Session, including deferred replies that still hold a lease. Defaults to 1.

join_token.description: Required by a network Runtime; omitted for trusted embedded join.

identity_proof.description: EdDSA JWT required by a network Runtime.

delivery_history.description: How Deliveries to this Session carry Thread history. Omit for `bodies`. `ids` is for an Agent that pages history itself and does not want Message copies on every Delivery.

JoinRequest.description: Input that creates or reconnects a Membership and opens one Instance.

AgentName.description: Agent name input. Length 1 to 63. The Runtime canonicalizes ASCII uppercase to lowercase; `-` and `_` are allowed only between alphanumeric characters.

max_message_bytes.description: Maximum accepted size in bytes of a `send` or `reply` body's UTF-8 JSON encoding. A larger body fails with `payload_too_large`. HTTP applies the same budget to every JSON request body before fully buffering it. The budget also caps a Delivery `history` window of Message bodies.

max_mailbox_depth.description: Maximum queued plus leased items one Membership Mailbox holds before `send` returns `busy`. The Runtime enforces this as an exact count.

delivery_history_limit.description: Maximum earlier Thread Messages the Runtime includes in a Delivery's `history` window. Older Messages are paged with `get_history`. The window is also truncated so its UTF-8 JSON encoding does not exceed `max_message_bytes`.

wait_hold_seconds.description: Seconds a `collect=wait` `send` may stay open. When this elapses and the Ticket is still `open`, `send` returns that Ticket and the Client continues with `get_result`. `0` returns immediately after acceptance.

max_held_waits.description: Maximum concurrent `collect=wait` sends one Membership may hold. A further `send` with `collect=wait` fails with `wait_limit`. `busy` remains the Mailbox-full error. `0` refuses every held wait.

work_lifetime_seconds.description: Seconds of work the Runtime stamps on a new request whose send omitted `deadline` and that has no request parent to inherit from. This is a cutoff, not a completion estimate or a promise that the recipient will finish. A child request cannot exceed its request parent's stamped deadline. MUST NOT exceed `max_deadline_seconds`.

max_deadline_seconds.description: Maximum seconds from acceptance until a new request `deadline`. An explicit deadline further in the future fails with `invalid_request`.

max_open_tickets.description: Maximum open Tickets one Membership may have as requester. A further new request fails with `busy`. Replays of accepted work do not consume another slot.

replay_horizon_seconds.description: Seconds after an obligation ends during which an identical `send`, `reply`, or `complete` retry returns the original result. For a request that interval starts when the Ticket becomes terminal and is taken as the later of this duration after close and the Ticket `deadline`. For an event it starts at acceptance. After it ends the Runtime MAY delete the replay record. The id may be used for new work only when no Delivery, Ticket, Thread history entry, or replay record still names it.

max_retained_bytes.description: Maximum UTF-8 JSON bytes of retained Message bodies this Runtime keeps. A new `send` or `reply` that would pass the cap fails with `busy`. Live work, Ticket and replay windows, and remaining Thread history stay.

RuntimeLimits.description: Fixed operational limits a Runtime reports at join.

session_token.description: Bearer credential for the new Session.

address.description: Canonical qualified Address assigned to the Membership.

team_name.description: Canonical name of the Team served by this Runtime.

agent_did.description: Verified identity bound to the Membership.

instance_id.description: Instance id for this Session, assigned when the Client omitted one.

spec_version.description: Exact public contract version implemented by the Runtime.

SessionToken.description: Opaque non-empty bearer credential returned by join.

TeamName.description: Lowercase Team name and valid DNS label. Length 1 to 63.

PersistenceMode.description: How a Runtime survives process exit. `durable` means a Runtime process restart recovers retained store data. Redis server crash and replica failover are deployment configuration, not this value.

session_expires_at.description: Current Session expiry after the heartbeat.

HeartbeatResult.description: Result of a successful Session heartbeat.

id.description: Client-generated Message id and idempotency key. The Runtime stores this value as the accepted Message `id`.

thread_id.description: Optional conversation grouping id.

parent_id.description: Optional Message this send replies to or continues.

metadata.description: Sender-controlled data that never changes Runtime decisions.

collect.description: How the sender collects the result. `wait` or `ticket`.

deadline.description: Future absolute work cutoff for the Ticket. Omit to inherit a request parent's stamped deadline, or to receive `now` plus `work_lifetime_seconds` for a root request. This is a cutoff, not a completion estimate.

RequestSendRequest.description: Send a request. Always opens a Ticket. `collect` is required. `deadline` may be omitted: the Runtime fills it at acceptance from the request parent or from `work_lifetime_seconds`. The accepted Message and Ticket always carry that effective cutoff. Fire-and-forget work is `EventSendRequest`.

id.description: Client-generated Message id and idempotency key. The Runtime stores this value as the accepted Message `id`.

thread_id.description: Optional conversation grouping id.

parent_id.description: Optional Message this send replies to or continues.

metadata.description: Sender-controlled data that never changes Runtime decisions.

status.description: Discriminator for a send that created no Ticket.

ticket.description: Current Ticket. Immediate `collect=ticket` and an elapsed `wait` hold both return this wrapper; `state` may be `open` or terminal. Completion is read from the Ticket, not from this result wrapper.

max_items.description: Number requested, from 1 to 100. Defaults to 1.

deliveries.description: Zero or more newly leased attempts.

LeaseResult.description: Deliveries currently leased to the Session.

lease_id.description: Active lease owned by the calling Session.

RenewRequest.description: Input to extend one active Delivery lease.

lease_expires_at.description: New time after which this attempt is no longer active.

CompleteRequest.description: Finish one Delivery without a response. For an event this just ends the Delivery. For a request it declines the request: the recipient chose not to answer, and the Ticket becomes `declined`.

ticket.description: Present only when completing a request, which declines it.

id.description: Client-generated id for the response or error Message. Replay equality includes this id, the target request Message id, and the outcome data. `lease_id` authorizes the attempt and is not part of that equality.

lease_id.description: Active lease for the reply-expected request. It authorizes this attempt and is not the durable identity of the reply.

content.description: Successful application result. Use null to answer with no content.

ReplySuccessRequest.description: Complete a Delivery with successful content.

id.description: Client-generated id for the response or error Message. Replay equality includes this id, the target request Message id, and the outcome data. `lease_id` authorizes the attempt and is not part of that equality.

lease_id.description: Active lease for the reply-expected request. It authorizes this attempt and is not the durable identity of the reply.

ReplyFailureRequest.description: Complete a Delivery with a safe error.

ticket.description: Terminal Ticket containing the accepted outcome.

ticket_id.description: `ticket_id` from `ask`. Equal to the request Message id. Repeat while `state` is `open`. Ending a wait does not cancel work.

GetResultRequest.description: Ticket lookup used by non-HTTP bindings. Collects a saved request result.

thread_id.description: Thread whose retained Messages are read. Only a participant may read it.

before.description: Return Messages older than this Message id, exclusive. Omit for the newest page. Prefer `next_before` from the previous page over picking an id from `messages`. A well-formed UUID that is not in the retained transcript, including an evicted id, returns the newest page. A non-UUID value is `invalid_request`.

limit.description: Page size from 1 to 200. Defaults to 50.

messages.description: Requested page ordered by `seq` ascending. The newest page is returned first, but order inside the page is oldest to newest.

has_more.description: True when older retained Messages remain before this page.

next_before.description: Pass this as the next `before` to load the older page. Present when `has_more` is true and `messages` is not empty; equal to `messages[0].id`. Omit `before` when `has_more` is false; do not loop on the same cursor.

HistoryResult.description: One page of retained Thread history.

id.description: Message id. `HistoryView.next_before` is the paging cursor.

seq.description: Thread sequence. History is ordered by `seq` ascending inside a page.

created_at.description: When the Runtime accepted this Message.

id.description: Message id. `HistoryView.next_before` is the paging cursor.

seq.description: Thread sequence. History is ordered by `seq` ascending inside a page.

created_at.description: When the Runtime accepted this Message.

id.description: Message id. `HistoryView.next_before` is the paging cursor.

seq.description: Thread sequence. History is ordered by `seq` ascending inside a page.

created_at.description: When the Runtime accepted this Message.

id.description: Message id. `HistoryView.next_before` is the paging cursor.

seq.description: Thread sequence. History is ordered by `seq` ascending inside a page.

created_at.description: When the Runtime accepted this Message.

parent_id.description: Request Message id this reply answers. Same value as that ask's `ticket_id`.

HistoryResponseTurn.description: Successful reply turn on a model-facing history page.

id.description: Message id. `HistoryView.next_before` is the paging cursor.

seq.description: Thread sequence. History is ordered by `seq` ascending inside a page.

created_at.description: When the Runtime accepted this Message.

parent_id.description: Request Message id this error answers. Same value as that ask's `ticket_id`.

HistoryErrorTurn.description: Failed reply turn on a model-facing history page.

HistoryTurn.description: One history turn. Discriminated on `kind`. MCP `get_history` and Session-bound Team tools return these instead of wire Messages.

messages.description: Requested page ordered by `seq` ascending. The newest page is returned first, but order inside the page is oldest to newest.

has_more.description: True when older retained Messages remain before this page.

next_before.description: Pass this as the next `before` to load the older page. Present when `has_more` is true and `messages` is not empty; equal to `messages[0].id`.

HistoryView.description: Model-facing Thread history page. Same paging contract as `HistoryResult`. Runtime, HTTP, and Client `get_history` still return `HistoryResult`.

query.description: Natural-language description of the work. Ranked matches are candidates, not proof that someone is suitable.

limit.description: Maximum results from 1 to 100. Omit to return every remaining member, capped at 100.

matches.description: Matches ordered by relevance, best first.

addresses.description: Member Addresses to read. One to 20. Result items follow this order after duplicate requested strings are dropped, keeping the first.

deadline_seconds.description: Relative work cutoff from 1 to 86400 seconds. Omit to inherit a request parent's stamped deadline, or to receive the Runtime work lifetime on a root request. This cuts off work; it is not how long `ask` waits.

collect.description: How long this `ask` call waits. Defaults to `wait`. Same closed set as Runtime `send` and Client `ask`. `wait` holds until the Ticket is terminal or `wait_hold_seconds` elapses, then returns the current saved request result, which may still be `open`. `ticket` returns immediately. Neither cancels work. While `state` is `open`, call `get_result`; do not send a second `ask`.

thread_id.description: Conversation to continue with the same recipient (a current Thread participant). Omit to start a conversation; that is the usual path. The server then mints a Thread id and the saved request result carries it. A well-formed unused id also starts a conversation. A Thread's participant set is fixed at creation. Another peer cannot join it (`forbidden`); omit `thread_id` and put needed context in `content`.

idempotency_key.description: Stable key so a retried tool call does not create a second request. When present, the Message id is UUID5 of `ask|<caller_address>|<idempotency_key>`. Equivalent retries reuse the original generated Thread and absolute deadline. Changed recipient, content, collect, or supplied `thread_id` fail with `id_conflict`. Retry identical arguments, or use a new key only for new work; do not drop the key after an uncertain accept. When omitted, the server mints a fresh UUID.

AskToolRequest.description: MCP `ask` arguments. The server generates the request Message id.

content.description: Event data. Text or JSON. `tell` never creates a Ticket.

thread_id.description: Conversation to continue with a current participant. Omit for an unthreaded notice; that is the usual path. Another peer cannot join an existing Thread (`forbidden`); omit `thread_id` and put needed context in `content`.

idempotency_key.description: Stable key so a retried tool call does not create a second event. Same derivation rule as `AskToolRequest.idempotency_key`. Equivalent retries return the original accepted event. Changed recipient, content, or `thread_id` fail with `id_conflict`. Retry identical arguments, or use a new key only for new work; do not drop the key after an uncertain accept.

TellToolRequest.description: MCP `tell` arguments. The server generates the event Message id.

members.description: Every current Agent Membership. Principals, including `operator`, are omitted.

at.description: When the Runtime recorded the event.

trace_id.description: Causal id shared with the Messages in this operation.

actor.description: Membership that performed the step, or the requester for accept and open.

message_id.description: Message this step is about, when there is one.

parent_id.description: Parent Message of `message_id`, copied from that Message when recorded. Absent when that Message has no parent. A Client rebuilds the request tree from this field. `get_trace` still returns an ordered list.

ticket_id.description: Ticket this step is about, when there is one.

detail.description: Type-specific fields. `accepted` includes `kind`, `sender`, and `recipient`. `leased` includes `attempt`. `replied` includes `outcome` and `reply_id`. `ticket_closed` includes `state`. Unknown keys are ignored by a Client.

TraceEvent.description: One recorded step of a causal operation. `get_trace` returns these in the order the Runtime stored them.

TraceEventType.description:
Closed set of Trace timeline event types.

- `accepted`: the Runtime stored a Message.
- `ticket_opened`: a reply-expected request created a Ticket.
- `leased`: a Session took a Delivery.
- `completed`: `complete` finished the Delivery.
- `replied`: `reply` stored a response or error Message.
- `ticket_closed`: an open Ticket expired with no `reply` or `complete`.

online.description: True when the Membership has at least one unexpired Session in the store.

open_tickets.description: Open Tickets whose recipient is this Membership.

online.description: True when the Membership has at least one unexpired Session in the store.

StatusPrincipal.description: Principal Membership row in `status`. A principal has no Mailbox, so the row omits Mailbox depth and open-Ticket counts rather than reporting zero.

origin.description: HTTP origin when the Runtime is serving, for example `http://127.0.0.1:9000`. Omitted when it is not serving.

members.description: Every Membership, including principals such as `operator`. Ordered by Address.

name.description: Bind the token to this Agent name.

agent_did.description: Bind the token to this Agent DID.

ttl_seconds.description: Lifetime in seconds. Omit to use the Runtime default.

single_use.description: When true, a successful join consumes the token. Defaults to false.

IssueJoinTokenRequest.description: Operator input that creates a join token.

token.description: Secret the Agent sends as `join_token`. Keep it out of logs and Messages.

expires_at.description: Time after which this token cannot authenticate a join.

single_use.description: Whether a successful join consumes the token.

name.description: Bound Agent name, when the operator set one.

agent_did.description: Bound Agent DID, when the operator set one.

JoinTokenIssued.description: Operator view of a join token the Runtime just issued.

RevokeJoinTokenRequest.description: Operator input that revokes a join token.

RuntimeEvent.description: One event pushed on the Session event stream. `type` is open so new event types are added over time; a Client MUST ignore an unknown type. This draft defines `work_available`, whose `data` is `{}`, and `trace`, whose `data` is a `TraceEvent`.

ToolErrorResult.description: Structured MCP tool result when a Runtime operation fails. The MCP error flag is set. `error` is the unchanged Runtime `ErrorObject`. Readable text is `code: message`. Malformed arguments and authentication failures stay MCP-level errors, not this object.
